description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2022: Data-driven machine learning predictions of multi-hazard hurricane damage to buildings is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Maitane Olabarrieta, University of Florida (ufl.edu). The study presented here uses a data-driven machine learning framework that incorporates loading onto buildings via hurricane wind and surge intensity, load propagation through geospatial features, and load resistance dependent on building components. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-6vmy-n836. Keywords: hurricanes, machine learning, damage prediction. Published 2023-03-20. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
